title: Janus-induced atomic reconstruction amplifies twist-angle modulation of interlayer thermal transport in moiré bilayers
authors: Bin Xu, Rulei Guo, Jie Sun, Hiroo Suzuki, Takuma Yoshida, Ichiro Nakaya, Koki Sawasaki, Yasuhiko Hayashi, Shohei Chiashi, Tomoki Machida, Junichiro Shiomi
abstract: In two-dimensional moiré bilayers, atomic reconstruction, the spontaneous structural relaxation toward energy-minimizing stacking registries in the near-commensurate regime, can strongly modify local stacking and interlayer coupling, providing a possibility to significantly control phonon-mediated properties. Here we show that the twist-angle dependence of interlayer thermal conductance can be modified by introducing Janus-induced mirror-symmetry breaking into bilayer MoS2. The intrinsic out-of-plane dipole in MoSSe/MoS2 bilayers leads to frictionless interface, and reduces the lattice deformation energy, thereby promoting atomic-reconstruction into locally distorted aperiodic moiré patterns. These features weaken interlayer coupling and suppress phonon transmission across the interface, leading to an anomalously strong twist-angle dependence of thermal conductance, with a pronounced minimum at small twist angles and a reduction rate nearly one order of magnitude larger than that of twisted bilayer MoS2. Our results demonstrate that interlayer thermal transport is modified by atomic reconstruction, highlighting Janus-induced mirror-symmetry breaking as an effective way to promoting phonon engineering in two-dimensional moiré structures.
summary: This work demonstrates that introducing a dipole asymmetry (Janus effect) into $	ext{MoSSe/MoS}_2$ moiré bilayers dramatically enhances the sensitivity of interlayer thermal transport to twist angle. This enhanced tunability is attributed to atomic reconstruction, which weakens interlayer coupling and suppresses phonon transmission in a highly predictable manner.
main_problem: The study aims to understand how atomic reconstruction, driven by Janus-induced symmetry breaking, modifies the twist-angle dependence of interlayer thermal transport in moiré bilayers.
main_result: Janus functionalization leads to an anomalously strong and highly tunable twist-angle dependence of thermal conductance, characterized by a pronounced minimum at small twist angles.
method: The research combines experimental measurements (TDTR for thermal conductivity, Raman/PL spectroscopy) with theoretical calculations (DFT modeling of structural relaxation and charge density).
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{MoSSe/MoS}_2$ moiré bilayers, which are Janus 2D materials exhibiting an intrinsic out-of-plane dipole. The physics involves atomic reconstruction into locally distorted aperiodic moiré patterns.
key_observables: Interlayer thermal conductance ($	ext{TC}$), low-frequency Raman modes (breathing mode frequency), and charge density distribution/Bader net atomic charges.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), small twist angles ($0^\circ - 5^\circ$), and the presence of the Janus dipole moment.
main_assumptions: The rigid stacking model is used for periodicity estimation, but the core mechanism relies on structural relaxation (atomic reconstruction) which deviates from this ideal assumption.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $	ext{TC}$ vs. twist angle showing minima; Raman/PL maps confirm Janus conversion; DFT results show charge density changes linked to interlayer coupling strength.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the structural difference (Janus effect) compared to homo-bilayers, then measuring the resulting $	ext{TC}$ modulation experimentally, and finally using DFT calculations and spectroscopic analysis to link this strong tunability directly to atomic reconstruction pathways.
why_interesting: While focused on thermal transport, the mechanism—controlling interlayer coupling via symmetry breaking (dipole) leading to structural phase transitions (reconstruction)—is analogous to controlling quantum coupling strengths in engineered quantum materials or interfaces.
